title: Olfactory stimuli and moonwalker SEZ neurons can drive backward locomotion in Drosophila.
source_locator: Results 'Optogenetic activation of GH146II-, NP225-, and NP5288-GAL4 triggers backward walking'; Fig. 2C, 2E-H; Fig. S2A
quote: Activation of MDNs using both the broad and narrow MDN driver lines indeed elicited sustained backward walking, as previously observed18 (Figure S2A).
mapping_basis: Paper names the neurons moonwalker descending neurons (MDNs); MDN is the MANC type name.
sensory_condition: open arena (60 mm), freely walking groups of 3-15 flies, IR illumination
coordination_notes: sustained, straight backward walking with weak angular change (Fig. 2C)
penetrance: Fig. 2H: most VT50660>XXM flies walked >=3 mm backward during the 2-s pulse
notes: Called the 'broad MDN driver line' VT50660-GAL4 (VT050660-GAL4 attP2); other labelled cells not named in this paper. Centroid tracking (Ctrax) of translational velocity; legs not tracked individually; backward walking coded yes for all leg pairs per convention. effect_on_walking 'slows' chosen because forward translational velocity reverses to backward walking (no exact vocabulary term).

title: Olfactory stimuli and moonwalker SEZ neurons can drive backward locomotion in Drosophila.
source_locator: Fig. 3B (light-green trace, VT50660-GAL4>UAS-CsChrimson, MDN-LexA without LexAop-TNT); Video S3
quote: TNT in MDNs completely blocks backward walking
mapping_basis: Paper names the neurons MDNs; MDN is the MANC type name.
notes: figure: Fig. 3B shows that without TNT (VT50660-GAL4>UAS-CsChrimson, MDN-LexA) translational velocity drops from ~+3 to about -5 to -10 mm/s during the 2-s red pulse (mean ~-5 mm/s). This is the positive-control activation; the quote states the TNT contrast. Text: 'As a positive control, the efficiency of the LexAop-TNT was confirmed by direct optogenetic activation of MDNs.' effect_on_walking 'slows' = forward velocity reversed to backward.
